title: activation-concordance-and-cross-team-closure-protocol-wip
body:
Purpose: outline a lightweight operational pattern to ensure the signals we rely on during evaluation (offline/QA) and canary runs align with production user behavior, and define a cross-team closure protocol so launches are not 'handed off' with ambiguous ownership. This is a working sketch — many TODOs below.

Context / motivation:
- We keep seeing launches where evaluation metrics (eval set, synthetic traffic) look fine but production signals diverge (latency spikes, higher hallucination rate on long prompts, unexpected slice regressions).
- Problem often: mismatch in traffic composition, request payload shapes, or observability gaps (we measured model quality but not reranker fairness).
- Goal: reduce surprise failures by (1) codifying a quick concordance checklist to run pre-canary and during early exposure, and (2) an explicit cross-team closure protocol so Product / Eng / SRE / Trust / CS sign off on activation state.

What is "activation concordance" (working def):
- A compact set of checks that compares evaluation baseline signals to short-window production signals along critical axes: request shape, token length distribution, model latency percentiles, top-k ranking changes, safety flags, and cost per thousand tokens.
- Concordance is not exact equality. We assert tolerances per-signal (examples below) and a small handoff window where humans inspect anomalies.

Quick checklist (pre-canary gate):
- Data + traffic parity: sample production sandbox traffic (if available) and confirm schema matches (fields, optional args, max_tokens). If no sandbox, generate synthetic traffic using production examples stored in secure bucket.
- Metric set defined and instrumented: latency_p50/p95, tokens_per_request, requests_with_tools_percent, safety_flag_rate, rerank-shift-rate, downstream_error_rate.
- Baseline values: attach baseline numbers from evaluation and last successful release (link).
- Instrumentation smoke: run test queries through monitoring pipeline and confirm traces show up in the same dashboards as real traffic (trace ids, service name).
- Alert hooks configured: at least one slack channel + pager rota for rapid rollback.
- Rollout policy defined: start fraction, doubling cadence (e.g., 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%), hold windows, maximum time per step.
- Fallback plan: model variant to fall back to and capacity confirmation.

Concordance checks to run during first 24–72 hours of exposure:
- Shape parity: compare distribution of request field presence and average prompt length. Tolerance: +-15% on median token length, +-5% on presence of optional fields (e.g., user_metadata).
- Latency alignment: p95 production should be within +25% of eval p95. If >25%, invoke latency response play (see infra runbook).
- Quality alignment (proxy): top-level quality proxy (e.g., rerank-shift-rate) should not degrade >3 percentage points vs baseline.
- Safety signals: safety_flag_rate must be <= baseline + 0.5 percentage points or absolute 0.1% (whichever more conservative).
- Cost per 1k tokens: must remain within budgeted delta (configurable per feature).
- Downstream error amplification: monitor downstream system errors that correlate with model responses (e.g., parser failures). Any >2x increase -> halt.

Example concordance dashboard queries (pseudo):
- SELECT percentile_latency(request_id, 95) GROUP BY model_variant, region 
- SELECT avg(token_count) WHERE model_variant='rerank-v2' LAST_24H
- SELECT count(*) FILTER (safety_flag=true) / count(*) GROUP BY slice
- Compute shadow-rerank divergence: fraction of requests where shadow variant top1 != prod top1

Signal discordance triage flow (fast):
- If a single non-safety signal violates threshold: traffic steward notes event, notify product and infra, hold next exposure step for manual review.
- If safety signal violated: immediate rollback to previous stable variant + incident declaration + trust escalation.
- If multiple signals cross moderate thresholds: reduce to previous safe fraction (or 0.1%) and run synthetic replay on fresh production samples.

Roles and responsibilities (minimal):
- Rollout Owner (product/PM): coordinates decision, owns customer comms, prioritizes test cases.
- Traffic Steward (rotating): runs concordance checks, executes exposures in console, initiates rollback.
- Observability Lead (SRE/infra): validates telemetry, adjusts dashboards, performs low-level mitigations (throttle, scale).
- Evaluation Owner (applied-ml): provides baseline metrics, crafts targeted eval prompts for failing slices.
- Trust & Safety contact: responds to safety flags and coordinates triage.
- CS/Early Access rep: surfaces customer reports and helps prioritize remediation.

Cross-team closure protocol (what we require before marking a rollout as "closed"):
- 72-hour stability window with no major signals breached at the final exposure fraction OR steady-state at least 7 days with <1 moderate alert per day.
- Post-launch evidence pack submitted by rollout owner: concordance dashboard snapshot, sample failure cases, root-cause hypothesis, mitigation steps taken if any, and ticket list for follow-up work.
- Runbook: ownership of any open issues assigned with SLAs (P0/P1).
- Customer comms: if feature was gated for customers or is an external change, note who will author postmortem and messaging.
- Formal signoffs: short approval note in the rollout thread from Product, SRE, Applied-ML, Trust & Safety, and CS. Stored in linked artifacts.

Example minimal closure note (template):
- "Closure: rerank-v2 rolled to 100% on 2026-02-20. 7d stab. No safety breaches. Latency p95 within +8% vs baseline. 3 low-priority follow-ups (JIRA-1102, -1103, -1105). Signoffs: Asha (prod), Diego (SRE), Meera (Applied ML), K. Liu (Trust)."

Operational play snippets (quick ops):
- Emergency rollback: traffic steward flips route to model:rerank-v1 and pins traffic to dedicated capacity. Create incident channel, tag SRE and PM.
- Partial rollback: reduce exposure fraction to 1% and enable shadow logging for 24h, run perturbation eval for suspect slices.
- Hotfix push: if model behavior fix is a prompt/template change, gate change behind canary with shorter hold (24h) and more aggressive telemetry.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
- (P0) Where do we persist the concordance baselines? current idea: attach baseline artifact to each release in infra/artifacts (link). Need a small schema.
- (P1) Should we run automatic shadow-comparison telemetry for every canary, or only for deploys that touch reranking/structured outputs? Cost tradeoffs.
- (P1) Formalize tolerances per-team (SRE cares about latency, Product cares about downstream UX metrics). Short-term: keep a single default tolerance and allow overrides.
- (P2) Draft a minimal dashboard template + queries for the canary checklist (Meera to own).
- (P2) Add a small template for customer-facing comms for partial rollbacks.

Meeting cadence and artifacts during rollout (suggested):
- Pre-launch alignment (15–30m): Product + SRE + Applied-ML + Trust review checklist, set owner and steward.
- Canary daily check-in (10m) for first 3 days if >10% traffic; else check every other day. Traffic steward posts concordance snapshot in thread.
- Closure review (30m) when meeting the closure criteria; capture signoffs and attach evidence pack.

Example small-run canary sketch (rerank-v2):
- Pre-checks: baseline attached, console route ready, fallback variant rerank-v1 validated, synthetic traffic bucket loaded with 1k recent queries.
- Exposure: 0.5% -> hold 4h -> 2% -> hold 8h -> 10% -> hold 24h -> 50% -> hold 48h -> 100%.
- Watches: p95 latency, safety_flag_rate, rerank-shift-rate, downstream_parse_errors.
- Rollback triggers: safety_flag_rate > baseline + 0.1% OR rerank-shift-rate degradation >5pp OR p95 latency > +50%

Notes to self / voice-of-author:
- Keep this doc short and prescriptive; we have many long playbooks. The unique value is the cross-team closure artifact and the concordance framing.
- We should prototype on the small reranker rollouts first and iterate.

Signatures / next steps (short):
- Meera to create basic dashboard + queries by 2026-03-12.
- Diego to sketch traffic steward rota and brief the on-call team 2026-03-16.
- Asha to trial this on rerank-v2 canary next week; capture evidence pack in linked_artifacts.

Links: (placeholder) Confluence draft, JIRA queue, infra PR where route toggles live.
